notes: Real-repository corpus (internal/corpus). v3 gives the corpus GO DEPTH: six pinned Go repositories (uuid, lo, cobra, gin, grpc-go, kubernetes) carry the P0 FR-2 stratification, beside the non-Go repositories kept for cross-language regression detection (flask, sinatra, ky, express, guava, and okio — the first Kotlin pin, language-GA program G5). Refs pin RELEASE TAGS; sha additionally pins the checkout HEAD (case-insensitive prefix, >=12 hex chars — the Go entries pin the FULL 40-char commit sha). If an upstream tag is ever re-pointed, the pin step fails closed. Every count under `measured` was taken from a real clone at the pinned sha on the recorded date, never from repository metadata; `go_files` is the strict count the stress threshold is asserted on, and `source_files` is its non-Go analog (the entry's primary-language source count). Tiers: 1 = PR gate (local fixtures), 2 = pinned SHAs, 3 = nightly/manual, 4 = manual-only stress (corpus.yml caps the scheduled run at -max-tier 3, so tier 4 never runs on a schedule or a PR). Adding a repository is a data change here, never a code change. Per-repository selection rationale: corpus/README.md.

stratification.evidence: 21 Go files in a single package, 31 tracked files — the smallest real repository in the corpus.
36 Go files in 2 packages; the CLI framework plus its doc generator, with 17 test files.
92 Go files in 7 packages; HTTP router, middleware chain, binding and render subpackages.
831 Go files spread over 277 directories containing Go source.
15718 Go files over 3611 package directories; staging/ alone holds 5899 of them as separately published modules.
13 of 17 Go files declare type-parameterised functions over any/comparable constraints.

11 go.mod files (root plus examples, interop, security, stats and cmd submodules). Asserted on grpc-go rather than kubernetes (34 go.mod) because grpc-go runs on the nightly tier, so the property is exercised without the stress target.
16 Go files carry //go:build constraints (nomsgpack, jsoniter, sonic, go1.20+ variants).
49 Go files carry the "Code generated ... DO NOT EDIT" marker (protobuf and grpc plugin output).
287 _test.go files, 13 of which declare Benchmark functions.

entries.name: okio
entries.permitted_use: Public repository under Apache-2.0; the corpus shallow-clones it read-only in CI and publishes measurements only — no source is redistributed.

measured.method: git clone --depth 1 --branch 3.9.1; git ls-files '*.kt' '*.java' | wc -l (284 kt + 29 java = 313) and git ls-files | wc -l at the pinned sha 8b870e8

jvm_compile.reason: NEGATIVE RESULT (AC-7), and a precise one: okio's JVM source set COMPILES — that was proven, not assumed — but it cannot be compiled IN THE LAYOUT THIS ORACLE REQUIRES, so within this pipeline the pin is not compiled and does not back the corpus-scale claim. The oracle keys a call on the callee's source path, and javap supplies that path from the SourceFile attribute, which carries only the file NAME plus the package. okio's Kotlin-multiplatform expect/actual layout gives 18 package-relative paths TWO claimants each (okio/Buffer.kt exists in both commonMain and jvmMain, likewise BufferedSink, BufferedSource, ByteString, DeflaterSink, FileSystem, FileSystem.System, ForwardingSource, HashingSink, HashingSource, InflaterSource, Path, RealBufferedSink, RealBufferedSource, SegmentPool, SegmentedByteString, Sink, Timeout), covering 36 of the 89 files in the JVM source-set closure. Keeping one claimant of a pair would attribute the other's calls to the survivor — a fabricated fact, stop-ship under D5. Excluding all 36 leaves 53 files that DO NOT COMPILE, because the expect and actual halves are each other's dependencies. So okio is compilable-but-unscorable or scorable-but-uncompilable, and neither state is evidence. Recorded here rather than dropped, per AC-7. Unblocking it needs a capture that carries the FULL source path — `javap -v`'s SourceDebugExtension, or compiling each source set to its own output tree and keying on that — which is a capture-strategy change beyond this story.
tried: kotlinc 1.9.24 over commonMain+jvmMain only, in the pin's NATURAL layout: FAILED, 15 errors, all 'actual X has no corresponding expected declaration' — the JVM target's source-set closure is wider than two directories.

kotlinc 1.9.24 over the FULL closure read from okio/build.gradle.kts (jvmMain dependsOn zlibMain + systemFileSystemMain, both dependOn commonMain), natural layout, -Xmulti-platform -Xexpect-actual-classes -Xcommon-sources: SUCCEEDED — 89 sources, 0 errors, 114 classes. This is why the pin is recorded as compilable; it is the scoring layout that defeats it.

kotlinc 1.9.24 over the same closure STAGED into the package-relative tree the oracle requires, with the 36 collision-affected files excluded: FAILED, 1158 errors, 0 classes — the expect and actual halves are each other's dependencies, so removing the ambiguity removes the program.

Gradle, the project's own build: FAILED at CONFIGURATION time with 'Unknown Kotlin JVM target: 21' — okio 3.9.1's Kotlin Gradle plugin predates JDK 21. Independently of that failure, a Gradle route resolves a transitive plugin set that cannot be digest-pinned, which is exactly the drift AC-1 forbids.

NOT tried, and named so the next attempt does not restart from zero: `javap -v` SourceDebugExtension (carries the full source path and would dissolve the collision), and per-source-set output trees keyed separately. Both are capture-strategy changes and belong to their own story.
jvm_compile.exclusion_reason: Not compiled in the oracle's required layout — see `tried`. MEASURED, not assumed: the staged compile fails with 1158 errors and 0 classes. The pin therefore backs no coverage figure, no counterexample count and no corpus-scale claim, and is excluded loudly rather than omitted silently.

compile_coverage.excluded_reason: Not compiled in the oracle's required layout — see `tried`. MEASURED, not assumed: the staged compile fails with 1158 errors and 0 classes. The pin therefore backs no coverage figure, no counterexample count and no corpus-scale claim, and is excluded loudly rather than omitted silently.

entries.notes: First Kotlin corpus pin (language-GA program G5): Square's okio, a Kotlin-multiplatform IO library (284 .kt + 29 .java at the pin). Tier 3 (nightly/manual, never the PR gate). Brings a non-Go entry to the v3 measured standard via the new source_files census field. Compile coverage (SW-190, PARITY-COV-001 closure): 0 of 89 staged sources compiled — 0.0000 — because the staging collisions reduce the staging set from 313 to 89 sources (36 expect/actual collisions dropped) but the remaining 53 are each other's dependencies; `compiled_files: 0` records the negative result honestly, the figure excludes zero silently exactly nowhere.

entries.name: kotlinx.serialization
entries.permitted_use: Public repository under Apache-2.0; the corpus shallow-clones it read-only in CI and publishes measurements only — no source is redistributed.

measured.method: git clone --depth 1 --branch v1.6.3; git ls-files '*.kt' '*.java' | wc -l (609 kt + 6 java = 615) and git ls-files | wc -l (974) at the pinned sha 3efe324b

jvm_compile.reason: kotlinx.serialization is the compiler-plugin case, and the plugin is exactly what makes it pinnable: kotlin-serialization-compiler-plugin is a single JAR on Maven Central, pinned here by URL+sha256 like any other artifact, so the 'transitively fetched compiler plugin' hazard is closed by data rather than trusted. The opt-in flags are not invented — they are read from the pin's own build.gradle and gradle/configure-source-sets.gradle (-opt-in=kotlin.ExperimentalMultiplatform, kotlin.ExperimentalStdlibApi, kotlinx.serialization.InternalSerializationApi, kotlinx.serialization.ExperimentalSerializationApi). Scope is core/ (commonMain + jvmMain): the formats/ modules add json/cbor/protobuf/hocon and their own dependencies, and each is a separate resolution question that would be answered separately rather than bundled into one figure. NOTE the toolchain skew, stated rather than hidden: the pin builds with Kotlin 1.9.22 (gradle.properties) and this strategy pins kotlinc 1.9.24, because 1.9.24 is the last 1.9.x and the plugin must match the compiler exactly. Both are exact versions, so the compile is reproducible; it is simply not byte-identical to what the project's own CI produced, and no claim here says it is.
jvm_compile.exclusion_reason: COMPILES AND IS REPRODUCIBLE; SCORING IS NOT YET ESTABLISHED, so this pin publishes no coverage figure and no counterexample count. What IS established and published: the compile (52 sources, 0 errors, 255 classes, kotlinc 1.9.24 + the digest-pinned serialization plugin) and its reproducibility (two independent runs, byte-identical capture digest e6d39791efb4203d35110f9952f3feb2cf40abf01a89680ba35df55eef23d599). What is NOT: the by-name differential reports 27 of 351 confirmed calls as unbacked (310 matched + 27 unbacked + 14 abstained = 351; by-arity and by-signature are VACUOUSLY sound, 0 judged of 1009 and 670 truth facts, all 351 abstaining under kotlin_bytecode_shape_unproven). CLASSIFICATION, RE-STATED IN SW-173 ROUND 1 — the first version of this field said the 27 were concentrated in two shapes and that classifying them was real work. Both halves were wrong: the reviewer classified all 27 in fifteen minutes, and the dominant mechanism was neither shape named. MEASURED against the pin's own source: 22 of 27 are Kotlin VALUE-CLASS (inline-class) name mangling, a SECOND mangling scheme in which kotlinc renames any function taking an inline-class parameter to `name-<hash>` and emits a bridge under the plain name, so the body's calls carry the mangled caller (serialize-2TYgG_w, deserialize-BwKQO78, toBuilder-GBYM_sE, writeContent-Coi6ktg, computeIfAbsent-gIAlu-s) while graphi answers `serialize`, which is what ValueClasses.kt:16 declares; 4 are an interface member lowered onto the implementing class through Encoder$DefaultImpls (graphi answers Encoding.kt:278, which is correct, and the bridge guard cannot catch it because parseClassHeader records extends and never implements); 1 is `internal` visibility mangling compounded with the value-class hash (append-7apg3OU$main). EVERY ONE IS THE ORACLE ACCUSING CORRECT CODE — none is a product defect, which is why none is filed as a JVMSOUND row; the value-class scheme is filed as JVMHARN-001 on the backlog and registered as AC-7 blind spot #18. JVMHARN-001 CLOSED 2026-08-23 (SW-188), IN THE HARNESS, which is where it lived: demangleValueClass in internal/jvmgroundtruth/groundtruth.go demangles `name-<hash>` on BOTH ParseJavap paths (caller attribution and callee naming), and the rewrite is accepted only when the plain name is declared as a member of the SAME class in the capture, the owner is in the capture, and the owner was compiled from a .kt file. Regressions, all green with no compiler present: internal/jvmgroundtruth/valueclass_test.go (TestValueClassBridgeName_MirrorsJVMResolve, TestDemangleValueClass_Guards, TestParseJavap_ValueClassCallerAndCallee -- confirmed RED with the two call sites removed -- and TestParseJavap_BackquotedDashNameIsNotRewritten) plus valueclass_drift_test.go (TestValueClassRule_IdenticalToJVMResolve, the source-identity guard on the rule this package copies verbatim from engine/jvmresolve, demonstrated RED on a divergence both mirrored tables stay green on; TestValueClassRule_CopySetIsClosed; TestValueClassRule_QualifiersResolveAlike). Product bytes do NOT move: internal/jvmgroundtruth is not linked by cmd/graphi, and ./cmd/graphi built -trimpath -buildvcs=false digests 0de6e64d6174f1793efbe8d3d0b2beb6561c3095a965f7ecdac3e86bfef46ebf before and after. READ THE NUMBERS IN THIS FIELD AS THEY STAND: none of them is re-measured by that closure. The by-name differential has NOT been re-run -- it needs kotlinc, absent from the local sandbox and installed unpinned from releases/latest only in the jvm-groundtruth workflow, so the re-run is a CI dispatch and is open work. The post-fix residual of 5 of 351 (the 4 Encoder$DefaultImpls interface-lowering rows plus the 1 compound append-7apg3OU$main, both of which the demangler provably declines) is a PROJECTION FROM THE HAND CLASSIFICATION ABOVE, NOT A MEASURED RESULT, and no surface may state it as measured until that dispatch publishes. SEPARATELY AND STILL OPEN: the by-arity/by-signature vacuity recorded above is NOT JVMHARN-001 and is untouched by its closure. All 351 sites abstain because internal/jvmgroundtruth/binder.go:236 returns kotlin_bytecode_shape_unproven unconditionally for every Kotlin site, before a single parameter is inspected -- a declared-Kotlin to JVM-descriptor mapping gap (nullability boxing, extension receivers, suspend continuations) filed as JVMHARN-003, whose prerequisite is pinning kotlinc by digest. Java is judged at three precisions; Kotlin at one. SW-173 closed four other such shapes after finding them here (synthetic bridge, anonymous-subclass constructor and its descriptor, sourceless multifile facade, multifile private-function mangling on both caller and callee), taking the count from 50 to 27 and guava from 7 violations to SOUND at all three precisions. THE SENTENCE THAT CLOSES THIS FIELD PREDATES THE JVMHARN-001 CLOSURE RECORDED ABOVE AND IS RETAINED UNCHANGED UNDER D6: when it was written the 27 were classified and none was fixed. As of 2026-08-23, 22 of the 27 are modelled by demangleValueClass in the harness and the residual is a PROJECTION of 5, not a measurement; the pin still publishes no coverage figure, and for the same reason it gave then -- the differential has not been re-run. The pin still publishes NO coverage figure: the 27 are now classified but not fixed, and a Kotlin coverage number read without JVMHARN-001 beside it would cover less than it appears to — the same rule AC-4 applies to a denominator.

entries.notes: Second Kotlin corpus pin (language-GA program G5, WP-J6): JetBrains' kotlinx.serialization, a reflectionless Kotlin-multiplatform serialization library (609 .kt + 6 .java at the pin; the 6 .java are module-info.java JPMS declarations, which carry no methods and produce no sites — expected). Tier 3 (nightly/manual, never the PR gate). Complements okio with a compiler-plugin-heavy, densely-generic Kotlin codebase for cross-language regression + JVM-binder breadth. Verified at pin time: graphi tables all 615 JVM files with ZERO parse or tabling crashes and the declared-type binder resolves 3517 typed Kotlin sites. SUPERSEDED 2026-08-19 (W1.b / SW-175), and the old sentence is kept above rather than overwritten because of what was wrong with it: 3517 is a NUMERATOR WITHOUT A DENOMINATOR — it says how many sites bound, never out of how many exist, which is the defect independent-review R6 named when it dropped Kotlin's recall threshold. The measured answer, same pin, same sha: the call-site binding rate is 19.16% = 2949 bound call sites / 15388 CST call sites (denominator counted by an INDEPENDENT tree-sitter walk, never from the binder), published with the full ten-reason skip histogram and every named exclusion in docs/rc/jvm-binding-rate.md. READ IT WITH ITS PARSE CAVEAT: the embedded tree-sitter Kotlin grammar leaves ERROR nodes in 80 of this pin's 609 .kt files (13.1%), so a recovered file still contributes a full denominator while the binder can no longer walk its bodies — guava's java equivalent is 0 of 621. The bias DIRECTION is measured and is anti-flattering: dirty parses DEPRESS the rate. Over the 529 cleanly-parsed files the rate is 21.15% (2908/13748); over the 80 dirty ones it is 2.50% (41/1640). An earlier version of this note said the direction was 'undetermined'; that was an incomplete measurement presented as an unavailable one and is retracted. SECOND FINDING: today's binder produces 3433 typed sites here (2949 call + 484 value), 84 FEWER than 3517, so the old numerator is not reproducible from this tree either — what it counted could not be determined, and the binder has changed since (ADR 0008 D6 corrected 2026-08-16 after JVMSOUND-001/002; SW-170 re-keyed the sweep). No attempt is made to reconcile the 84. Note the scope difference from the jvm_compile block above: the binding rate needs NO compiler and therefore covers ALL 615 files at the pin, not the 52 that compile. Compile coverage (SW-190, PARITY-COV-001 closure): 52 of 52 staged sources compile — coverage 1.0000 — measured 2026-08-21 against the post-SW-188 candidate. The 27 of 351 unbacked calls (the JVMHARN-001 value-class shape, recorded above) are a separate counterexample count, NOT bound to this figure: the figure answers 'does the source set compile', the unbacked calls answer 'does the binder's output agree with the bytecode'. A reader must read both to know the pin's evidence base.

entries.name: antlr4
entries.permitted_use: Public repository under the 3-clause BSD licence of The ANTLR Project; read-only shallow clone in CI, measurements only, no redistribution.

measured.method: git clone --depth 1 --branch 4.13.1; git ls-files '*.java' | wc -l (521) and git ls-files | wc -l (2269) at the pinned sha 7ed420ff2c78. NOTE the scope difference the JVM harness sees: internal/parity/jvmsource.go jvmSkipDir refuses any directory named `target`, and antlr4 has a SOURCE package of that name (tool/src/org/antlr/v4/codegen/target/, 10 .java files), so the JVM model discovers 511 of the 521 — measured, not assumed.

jvm_compile.reason: ACQUIRED BY SW-207 for one measured reason: it is the only pin in this corpus that hosts a NON-STATIC Java on-demand import, which is the source shape jvm_change_import_shadowing needs and which guava, okio and kotlinx.serialization between them do not contain (guava's single wildcard import is `import static java.util.stream.Collectors.*;`, a STATIC on-demand import that JLS 6.4.1's single-type rule does not govern). Its compile classpath is resolved completely and the resolution is EMPTY: runtime/Java/src is the ANTLR Java runtime and depends on nothing outside the JDK, so the classpath is complete by containing no artifact at all, and there is no resolver, no version range and no transitive discovery to drift. Scope is runtime/Java/src and stops there deliberately: the tool/ module needs StringTemplate 4, the antlr3 runtime, treelayout and javax.json, and the runtime-testsuite module needs junit5 and a per-target toolchain — each is a separate resolution question that would be answered separately rather than folded into one figure, exactly as kotlinx.serialization's formats/ modules are. Accept-errors was not needed: the staged compile reports ZERO errors.
jvm_compile.exclusion_reason: COMPILES AND IS REPRODUCIBLE; SCORING IS NOT ESTABLISHED, so this pin publishes a compile figure and NO counterexample count — kotlinx.serialization's disclosure shape, for a different reason. What IS established and published, measured 2026-08-23 on darwin-arm64/local-sandbox through internal/jvmcorpus's own TestPins path: the compile (174 of 174 offered sources staged, 0 errors, 214 classes, javac 21.0.6, EMPTY classpath) and its reproducibility (two independent runs from scratch, byte-identical capture digest 63f2a4537846fa467a7dee19e44e64f14d7a2b6b1ffd11ea2bfb7c11222374dc, 1886758 bytes, 1 javap shard). What is NOT: the signature-aware oracle over that capture reports SOUNDNESS FAILURES at all three precisions on the 1494 confirmed calls the binder produces over the 174 staged files — 4 unbacked confirmed calls with 37 abstained and 0 truth facts outside the recall denominator [by-name]; 4 unbacked with 53 abstained and 1 outside [by-arity]; 16 unbacked with 265 abstained and 286 outside [by-signature]. Those 24 rows are NOT classified and this story does not classify them: SW-207 acquires corpus SOURCE SHAPES for the WP-J7 parity matrix, and a parity row asserts full-vs-incremental byte-identity and needs no bytecode at all. Filed as JVMSOUND-ANTLR-001. Until it is answered, the pin backs NO counterexample count and NO corpus-scale claim, and the exclusion is recorded loudly rather than the pin being omitted silently (AC-7). Note what the exclusion does NOT retract: the compile_coverage figure below is a STAGING figure — 174 of 174 sources reach the compiler with no package-relative collision — and it is measured, reproduced by cmd/jvmcoverage on the runner's own path, and unaffected by the scoring question.

entries.notes: Third Java corpus pin, acquired by SW-207 (JVMCORPUS-001) to close the jvm_change_import_shadowing gap on the WP-J7 real-repository matrix. ANTLR 4's Java tool + runtime, BSD-3-Clause, 521 .java of 2269 tracked at the pin, zero .kt. WHAT IT IS FOR, stated so it is not read as general corpus breadth: it carries 58 NON-STATIC on-demand import STATEMENTS spread across 45 of the 511 .java files the JVM model sees (75 on-demand import statements in total, 17 of them static), which is the JLS 6.4.1 shape the row needs and which no other JVM pin has — measured 2026-08-23 by internal/parity's own model over a clone at 7ed420ff2c78, and re-measured 2026-08-23 in the review round by an independent grep over the same 511-file view, which agrees file-for-file. CORRECTED BY THE SW-207 REVIEW, ROUND 1: this sentence said `58 of its .java files`, publishing a STATEMENT count as a FILE count; 58 is statements, 45 is files. READ WITH PARITY-OBS-004: the pin genuinely has the shape, but planJVMChangeImportShadowing selects its target by unresolved token match, and the target it picks here (CustomDescriptors.java, imported name Lexer) carries all four of its `Lexer` tokens as `GrammarType.Lexer` member selects, so that particular row does not exercise JLS 6.4.1 re-resolution. The pin is not at fault and no predicate was changed. Compile coverage: 174 of 174 sources under runtime/Java/src stage without a single package-relative collision (one source root, so a collision is impossible by construction) and the staged compile reports 0 errors and 214 class files under javac 21.0.6 with an EMPTY classpath — measured 2026-08-23 on runner class darwin-arm64/local-sandbox against the unchanged 9f687849 candidate. EXCLUDED FROM THE CORPUS-SCALE CLAIM, and read the jvm_compile exclusion_reason before reading any figure here: the pin compiles and reproduces, but the signature-aware oracle reports 4/4/16 unbacked confirmed calls at by-name/by-arity/by-signature over 1494 confirmed calls, unclassified, filed as JVMSOUND-ANTLR-001. The parity rows this pin exists for do not depend on that: a real-repo parity row asserts full-vs-incremental byte-identity and never a correctness statement about an edge.

entries.name: retrofit
entries.permitted_use: Public repository under Apache-2.0; the corpus shallow-clones it read-only in CI and publishes measurements only — no source is redistributed.

measured.method: git clone --depth 1 --branch 2.11.0; git ls-files '*.kt' '*.java' | wc -l (300 java + 15 kt = 315) and git ls-files | wc -l (724) at the pinned sha cc76c22a68e0. The annotated tag 2.11.0 is object d3207228b7b8; the COMMIT it points at, and the value pinned here, is cc76c22a68e090f3dd898cbcb0bac30414f59c31.

jvm_compile.reason: NEGATIVE RESULT, MEASURED (AC-7), and the pin is acquired for a structural property rather than for a compile figure. SW-207 pins retrofit because it is the only repository examined that satisfies all five conjuncts of planJVMMixedDirChangeReceiverType: it holds four MIXED .java/.kt directories, and the class HttpException in retrofit-adapters/guava/src/main/java/retrofit2/adapter/guava/ is declared OUTSIDE all four, carries a supertype, is named by simple name from retrofit/kotlin-test/src/test/java/retrofit2/KotlinSuspendTest.kt INSIDE one of them, and has a sibling Java class (GuavaCallAdapterFactory) in its own directory to serve as the replacement supertype. The pin is NOT compiled, and that is measured three ways rather than assumed. (1) The natural scope retrofit/src/main/java is a MIXED-LANGUAGE module: its 55 staged sources are 54 .java plus retrofit2/KotlinExtensions.kt, and internal/jvmcorpus.Compile hands the WHOLE staged set to ONE compiler, so javac 21.0.6 aborts with `error: invalid flag: ./retrofit2/KotlinExtensions.kt` — exit 2, 0 class files. (2) The same 54 .java alone, with no classpath: 474 errors, 0 class files. (3) The same 54 .java alone with a Maven-Central classpath assembled from the pin's own gradle/libs.versions.toml (okhttp 3.14.9, okio 1.17.5, kotlin-stdlib 1.9.23, kotlinx-coroutines-core-jvm 1.8.0, animal-sniffer-annotations 1.23, jsr305 3.0.2): 24 errors, 0 class files, and every one of them is `package android.annotation does not exist` / `package android.os does not exist` / the symbols that follow from them. retrofit core compiles against android.jar as a compileOnly dependency; android.jar is NOT a Maven Central artifact and is distributed under the Android SDK licence, so no digest-pinned URL+sha256 classpath of the kind this strategy requires can be assembled for it. The pin therefore backs no coverage figure, no counterexample count and no corpus-scale claim, and is excluded loudly rather than omitted silently.
tried: javac 21.0.6 over the FULL staged set of retrofit/src/main/java (55 sources: 54 .java + retrofit2/KotlinExtensions.kt), with the digest-pinnable Maven Central classpath: FAILED, exit 2, `error: invalid flag: ./retrofit2/KotlinExtensions.kt`, 0 class files. Compile() passes every staged source to one compiler, and javac does not accept .kt.
javac 21.0.6 over the .java half only (54 sources), NO classpath: FAILED, 474 errors, 0 class files.

javac 21.0.6 over the .java half only (54 sources) with okhttp 3.14.9, okio 1.17.5, kotlin-stdlib 1.9.23, kotlinx-coroutines-core-jvm 1.8.0, animal-sniffer-annotations 1.23 and jsr305 3.0.2 on the classpath — every version read from the pin's own gradle/libs.versions.toml: FAILED, 24 errors, 0 class files, ALL of them android.annotation / android.os / android.os.Build. This is the decisive one: retrofit core declares `compileOnly libs.android`, and android.jar is not a Maven Central artifact and is not redistributable under the digest-pinned posture this strategy requires.

NOT tried, and named so the next attempt does not restart from zero: (a) kotlinc 1.9.24 over the same mixed staged set — it would accept the .java for resolution but emit class files for the ONE .kt only, so the oracle would score 1 of 55 sources and the pin would still back no figure; (b) scoping the compile to retrofit's pure-Java modules (retrofit-adapters/*, retrofit-converters/*) against a published com.squareup.retrofit2:retrofit jar — that compiles a module against the pin's own RELEASE ARTEFACT rather than the pin, which is a different measurement and would need its own decision; (c) adding android.jar to the classpath, which the licence posture in `permitted_use` does not allow.

entries.notes: Polyglot Java/Kotlin corpus pin, acquired by SW-207 (JVMCORPUS-001) to close the jvm_mixed_dir_change_receiver_type gap on the WP-J7 real-repository matrix. Square's retrofit, Apache-2.0, 300 .java + 15 .kt = 315 source files of 724 tracked at the pin. WHAT IT IS FOR: it is the only repository examined whose source satisfies the five-way conjunction planJVMMixedDirChangeReceiverType tests — four mixed .java/.kt directories (retrofit/src/main/java/retrofit2 27+1, retrofit-mock/src/main/java/retrofit2/mock 7+1, retrofit-mock/src/test/java/retrofit2/mock 4+1, retrofit/kotlin-test/src/test/java/retrofit2 3+2), 259 .java files outside them, 50 of those declaring a top-level class with a supertype, 6 of THOSE named by simple name from inside a mixed directory, and all 6 with a sibling Java class available as a replacement supertype. Measured 2026-08-23 by internal/parity's own model over a clone at cc76c22a68e0. READ CONJUNCT (4) LITERALLY, and see PARITY-OBS-004: `named by simple name` is referencesSimpleName, a whole-word TOKEN match with no import or package resolution. Measured in the review round at the same sha: retrofit declares SIX distinct classes named HttpException (retrofit2 plus the five retrofit2.adapter.{guava,java8,rxjava,rxjava2,rxjava3} packages), and the namer KotlinSuspendTest.kt is in package retrofit2 with no HttpException import, so its one HttpException token binds to retrofit2.HttpException — the SUPERCLASS of the edited retrofit2.adapter.guava.HttpException, not the edited class itself. The pin still hosts the SHAPE the conjunction tests; what it does not host is a resolved reference from inside a mixed directory to the edited type. Compile: NONE — see the jvm_compile block for the three measured attempts and why the pin backs no coverage figure. That is the okio disclosure shape and it costs the CLAIM, not the pin: retrofit's job here is to host a source SHAPE for a parity row, which needs no bytecode, because a real-repo parity row asserts full-vs-incremental byte-identity and never a correctness statement about an edge.

entries.name: tier1-fixture-hero-jvm
entries.notes: Tier-1 pinned multi-file JVM (Java+Kotlin) fixture for the WP-J6 hero-jvm tasks. The hero-jvm gate (cmd/eval/hero_jvm_test.go) sets GRAPHI_JVM_TYPERESOLVE and asserts the 12 stable ops over the CONFIRMED tier. This corpus smoke entry deliberately carries NO confirmed_edges assertion: the corpus runner drives the DEFAULT binary (binder off, JVM is Preview/heuristic), so a confirmed-edge assertion would be unsatisfiable here and would contradict the default-off contract. The heuristic search assertion is what the default product proves. No network, no JDK.

The hero-python gate (cmd/eval/hero_python_test.go) asserts the 12 stable ops over the HEURISTIC tier (engine/link/resolve_python.go), since Python has no typed binder — the G2SUB substitution is the language's honest level. The writers carry the heuristic resolver's from-import bare binding (`from impl.english import core`) so callers/callees/impact/related_files reach across modules at the heuristic tier. Negative anchor: org.salute (does NOT call core) must not appear in callers-of-core. No network, no Python interpreter.
